samples.title: Signed contract
samples.explanation: Alice signed it with a certificate from the trusted demo CA. Nothing changed afterwards.

samples.title: Amount changed after signing
samples.explanation: Someone edited Rs. 5,000 to Rs. 9,000 inside the PDF, so the hash no longer matches.

samples.title: Corrupted signature value
samples.explanation: One digit of the signature number s was changed, so s^e mod n no longer gives the hash.

samples.title: Content added after signing
samples.explanation: The signed part is intact, but extra bytes were appended afterwards, outside the signature.

samples.title: Self-signed certificate
samples.explanation: The maths is correct, but Mallory issued their own certificate, so nobody vouches for the name.

samples.title: Certificate from an untrusted CA
samples.explanation: Charlie's certificate chains to 'Unknown Root CA', which is not in our trust store.

samples.title: Expired certificate
samples.explanation: The certificate was valid only during 2023; it had expired when this was signed.

samples.title: Weak hash (SHA-1)
samples.explanation: The signature is correct, but SHA-1 collisions have been found, so it is no longer trusted.

samples.title: Unsigned PDF
samples.explanation: A normal PDF without any signature.

samples.title: PDF + PNG signature picture
samples.explanation: An existing PDF signed by Alice. Her PNG signature picture is shown in the box on the page; the real proof is the digital signature inside the PDF.

samples.title: PDF + JPEG signature picture
samples.explanation: The same PDF signed by Bob, with his JPEG signature picture.

samples.title: PDF + PNG, edited after signing
samples.explanation: The reason was changed from 'Project approved' to 'Project rejected' after signing. The picture still looks the same, but the hash no longer matches: a picture alone proves nothing.

samples.title: Existing PDF signed (no picture)
samples.explanation: An existing PDF signed without a picture; the box shows the signer's name and date.

samples.title: JPEG photo + .p7s
samples.explanation: Alice signed the JPEG image; the signature is in photo.jpg.p7s.

samples.title: JPEG photo edited after signing
samples.explanation: The year in the caption was changed from 2026 to 2027, so the JPEG bytes and their hash changed.

samples.title: PNG photo + .p7s
samples.explanation: Alice signed the PNG image; the signature is in photo.png.p7s.

samples.title: PNG photo edited after signing
samples.explanation: The year in the caption was changed from 2026 to 2027, so the PNG bytes and their hash changed.

samples.title: Text file with detached signature
samples.explanation: Bob signed the invoice; the signature is in a separate .p7s file.

samples.title: Edited text file
samples.explanation: The amount was changed after Bob signed, so the hash is different.

samples.title: Image with detached signature
samples.explanation: Any file is just bytes, so images can be signed too.

samples.title: Signature for a different file
samples.explanation: The photo's signature does not match the invoice.

samples.title: Signed message (.p7m)
samples.explanation: The text is stored inside the signature file itself (an 'enveloping' signature).
